data.title: Recurrent reversible mutations in gaf1 driving metastable TORC1 inhibitor resistance in fission yeast
data.authors: Dan L; Ye X; Liu S; Zhang J; Qiang Z; Yang X; Li W

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Metastable resistance to TORC1 inhibitors (rapamycin plus caffeine) in fission yeast is driven by recurrent, spontaneously reversible loss-of-function mutations in gaf1, a GATA transcription factor and negative growth regulator downstream of TORC1 - a genetic (not epigenetic) toggle that can silently contaminate lab yeast stocks.
data.abstract_excerpt: Metastable phenotypic inheritance is often attributed to epigenetic mechanisms, but reversible genetic alterations can produce similar instability. Here, we investigated the basis of unstable resistance to TORC1 inhibitor (rapamycin plus caffeine) in fission yeast. Six independent, metastable resistant mutants were isolated. Genetic mapping positioned the causal lesion to a single Mendelian locus, identified as gaf1, encoding a GATA transcription factor and a key negative regulator of growth downstream of TORC1.

extracted_findings.intervention: rapamycin plus caffeine selection; gaf1 loss-of-function and wild-type allele restoration
extracted_findings.target: TORC1 signalling output via the GATA transcription factor Gaf1
extracted_findings.effect: Reversible loss-of-function mutations in gaf1 were necessary and sufficient for metastable resistance to TORC1 inhibition, with derepression of translation and metabolic programmes on drug treatment.
